title: Power domination in the regular 4-polytopes
statement: A set S of vertices power dominates the graph when, starting from S and all neighbours of S as observed vertices, the rule 'an observed vertex with exactly one unobserved neighbour observes it' eventually observes every vertex; the power domination number is the smallest size of such a set. Determine the power domination number for the graphs of the six regular convex 4-polytopes (the 5-cell K5; the tesseract, 16 vertices; the 16-cell, 8 vertices; the 24-cell, 24 vertices, 8-regular; the 600-cell, 120 vertices, 12-regular; the 120-cell, 600 vertices, 4-regular) and of the two E8 polytopes 3_21 (Gosset, 56 vertices, 27-regular) and 4_21 (the 240 roots of E8, 56-regular), each vertex adjacent to its nearest neighbours. First values (ours): the 5-cell 1 (exact); the tesseract (8-cell) 2 (exact); the 16-cell 1 (exact); the 24-cell 2 (exact); the 600-cell 5; the 120-cell 28; the Gosset polytope 3_21 2; the E8 root polytope 4_21 6. The headline cell is the 120-cell: find a certificate with value 27 or less (Z(G) <= Delta * gamma_P(G) with the spectral bound for Z(G): >= 12 for the 120-cell), or prove 28 optimal.
submission: Text file: the vertex numbers of the set (spaces or newlines), in the checker's vertex order (the 120-cell).
score: the number of vertices in the set (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 28 for the 120-cell, best found: CP-SAT (one worker, 5 to 60 seconds) on the model of tools/polytope_sets.py, or, for zero forcing and power domination, greedy completion and pruning between rounds of fort cuts

context: Power domination models the placement of phase measurement units that monitor an electrical network (Haynes, Hedetniemi, Hedetniemi and Henning 2002); it is zero forcing started from a closed neighbourhood, so Z(G) <= Delta * gamma_P(G) and the spectral bound for zero forcing gives gamma_P >= (largest eigenvalue multiplicity) / Delta: at least 3 for the 600-cell, 12 for the 120-cell, 1 for 3_21 and 2 for 4_21. Values are known for grids, hypercubes and products; for these polytopes nothing was found.
references: T. W. Haynes, S. M. Hedetniemi, S. T. Hedetniemi, M. A. Henning, Domination in graphs applied to electric power networks, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 15 (2002) 519-529
K. F. Benson, D. Ferrero, M. Flagg, V. Furst, L. Hogben, V. Vasilevska, B. Wissman, Zero forcing and power domination for graph products, Australas. J. Combin. 70 (2018) 221-235
H. S. M. Coxeter, Regular Polytopes (3rd ed., Dover 1973)
the vertex numbering of checkers/orig_phys.py (polytope_graph), shared by every polytope problem of the Originals

novelty.verdict: new. No power domination result for the 600-cell, the 120-cell, the 24-cell or the E8 polytopes (searched with E8 and Gosset) was found on arXiv, in the journal literature (Crossref) or by web search; the known values for hypercubes and complete graphs cover only the small cells.
closest: General results on power domination (the references) and its values for hypercubes, grids and products; none for these polytopes.
Our polytope problems (polytope-ising, potts3-600, cell600-idcode, cell600-forest, cell120-coil, e8-idcode, e8-resolving): other invariants of the same graphs.

All cells: the 5-cell 1 (exact); the tesseract (8-cell) 2 (exact); the 16-cell 1 (exact); the 24-cell 2 (exact); the 600-cell 5; the 120-cell 28; the Gosset polytope 3_21 2; the E8 root polytope 4_21 6. Bound: 12 (Z(G) <= Delta * gamma_P(G) with the spectral bound for Z(G), for the 120-cell).
